chapter: Later tours, illness and the union job
title: Shaky nerves for weeks after slivovitch and rum
summary: Back in London he could barely walk or play for three weeks, with his jaws shaking in Copenhagen.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: So when I got back to London I was just a bundle of nerves, you know. Nothing but nerves and I got in like, like on a Sunday morning and I wanted so bad to go to sleep but I was too nervous to sleep. My nerves were just all shot. And I got
to bed about 10 o'clock. About 12 o'clock here comes Beryl Bryden to take me to a party.

She came by to take me to a party of all times. I could hardly walk. I just wanted to sit down. I sat down in the street once when we had to wait for a car. I just sat down. We got to the party and I got in a chair and I didn't move. I didn't want anything to eat, drink. And that lasted with me for about three weeks. I still was shaking in about three weeks.
Well did you drink an awful lot of it?

I think, I was drinking along with the tour. After a certain point I don't know what I was doing. After a certain point, me and all the guys were drinking rum and slivovitch together. And I went to Copenhagen three weeks later and I still was shaking. My jaws were shaking.
How could you play after a
I couldn't play, hardly, I couldn't.
Well I played but it was very shakey. (LAUGHTER). I played awful shakey.
It was rather an unusual lip vibrato or something.
